observed: engine/crates/membrane-updater::verify is pure fail-closed admission requiring both a Tauri updater signature (verify_tauri) and platform trust (verify_platform: macOS notarization, or Windows Public Trust + RFC3161) from a trusted UpdateTrustVerifier adapter before returning Ok(VerifiedUpdate); any failure returns Err(BlockedUpdate) carrying a stable failure-code list, the version pair, the artifact hash, and repair_path. Since the crate exposes no filesystem/process/download/activation API at all, a BlockedUpdate cannot have mutated anything -- the current version is preserved by construction, not by a separate rollback step. This task added the one real gap against the acceptance criterion that existed in the prior scaffold (commit 5cddb0b7): downgrade admission (FailureCode::DowngradeRejected, is_upgrade/version_triple), checked before either trust domain runs, so a stale-but-validly-signed artifact is refused without ever asking a trusted adapter to verify it. Rust #[test]s (reasoned, not executed) cover, one assertion each: dual valid signatures verify with zero failures; an empty Tauri signature blocks (InvalidEvidenceIdentity) and the receipt still names the preserved from/to version pair; an untrusted key_id blocks (TauriUpdaterSignatureInvalid); platform-signature-invalid-only blocks (PlatformSignatureInvalid); tauri-invalid-only blocks (TauriUpdaterSignatureInvalid) -- covering 'one valid signature out of two' both ways; platform-trust-invalid-only (e.g. codesigned but unnotarized) blocks (PlatformTrustInvalid); a downgrade with two fully valid signatures blocks (DowngradeRejected); an unparseable target version blocks the same way; a mismatched artifact hash between the Tauri and platform evidence records blocks (InvalidEvidenceIdentity); a malformed SHA-256 blocks; plus direct unit tests of version_triple/is_upgrade's parsing and comparison. apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/src/update_admission.rs is the runtime adapter that binds this gate to RightKit's real, already-produced output -- per the orchestrator's mid-task correction, it does not hand-roll or re-verify any signature cryptography: RightKitUpdaterManifestEntry deserializes exactly the {signature, url} shape tools/rightkit/packages/release/publish-update.mjs already emits (signed by sign-updater.mjs/create-mac-updater.mjs against the shared rightsuite-updater-key), and PlatformAcceptanceReceipt deserializes exactly the orthic.membrane.platform-acceptance.v1 schema scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs already defines and scripts/release/macos|windows/contract.mjs already build. Any RightKit output that fails to parse or is incomplete collapses to evidence membrane_updater::verify's own identity check is guaranteed to reject (empty key/signature/receipt id) rather than being treated as trusted-by-default. Its 8 reasoned tests cover: deserializing the real manifest-entry and full-receipt shapes (including tolerating unmodeled fields like lifecycle/environment); a full valid pair verifies; an untrusted updater key blocks; one failed trust field out of several (e.g. rfc3161: fail) blocks; a receipt for the wrong platform blocks; a downgrade with full trust blocks; a missing Tauri signature blocks; a mismatched artifact hash blocks. scripts/release/updater/contract.mjs mirrors this same fail-closed shape at release-orchestration time by importing (not duplicating) verify-platform-artifacts.mjs's validateReceipt, and its 12 tests (executed for real, see commands.log) exercise every one of the same cases directly against RightKit's real Windows manifest-entry and platform-acceptance-receipt shapes, plus that only the platform key RightKit's own right-release.config.mjs currently declares (windows-x86_64) is registered.
